market_definition: The bio-based adhesives market comprises adhesives whose polymer content is derived from renewable feedstocks other than starch and animal or plant proteins, such as lignin, tannin, cellulose derivatives, natural rubber and bio-based resins. It measures sales of finished bio-based formulations marketed on renewable content. BY FEEDSTOCK: Lignin & Tannin, Cellulose Derivatives, Natural Rubber & Rosin, Vegetable Oil & Bio-Polyol Based, Other Renewable Feedstocks. BY ADHESIVE TECHNOLOGY: Water-Based, Hot Melt, Reactive. BY END-USE INDUSTRY: Wood & Panels, Packaging, Hygiene & Consumer, Construction, Other End-Use Industries. BY REGION: North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia Pacific (APAC), Middle East, Africa. EXCLUDED from the market: Starch, dextrin and protein-based adhesives; petrochemical adhesives with minor renewable content; bio-based foams and tapes. COMPANY TYPE IN THIS LIST - DISTRIBUTOR: a distributor, stockist or specialty reseller that buys these products from their makers and sells them to industrial, construction or trade customers. EXCLUDED companies: product and raw-material makers and their own sales subsidiaries; companies selling only the excluded products; service-only firms. GEOGRAPHY OF THIS LIST: EUROPE - companies headquartered in a European country (EU, United Kingdom, EFTA, Western Balkans, Ukraine, Moldova, Russia).
who_is_included: DISTRIBUTOR DEFINITION (physical goods market): a company whose PRIMARY business is buying in volume from manufacturers and reselling/distributing onward - wholesale, authorized, value-added or stocking distributor.
